subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes and tangential differentials along C¹ charts (Simon Remarks 1.5(2), 1.8(1); Ch. 2 (4.8)-(4.10))
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ, p ∈ ℕ, N = n + ℓ. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be Hⁿ-measurable, θ a positive locally integrable weight on M (θ > 0 on M, θ is Hⁿ⌞M-measurable, ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K), U ⊇ M open, f : ℝ^N → ℝᵖ locally Lipschitz on U, V ⊆ ℝⁿ open and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N of class C¹ on V with injective derivative Dψ(u) at every u ∈ V. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ M: (A) M has approximate tangent space range Dψ(u) at ψ(u) with respect to θ in the sense of Simon's Definition 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt); (B) f ∘ ψ is differentiable at u; (C) for every w ∈ ℝⁿ, t ↦ f(ψ(u) + t·Dψ(u)w) has derivative D(f∘ψ)(u)w at t = 0 (HasLineDerivAt).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ p : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn (n + ℓ))) (θ : Rn (n + ℓ) → ℝ) (f : Rn (n + ℓ) → Rn p) (V : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn (n + ℓ)), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → (∀ u ∈ V, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ u)) → ∀ᵐ u ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), u ∈ V → ψ u ∈ M → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (ψ u) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ u).toLinearMap) ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u ∧ ∀ w : Rn n, HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u w) (ψ u) (fderiv ℝ ψ u w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Part (A) is Simon's Remark 1.5(2) (chapter-03.txt lines 87-90), proved in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (lines 113-143), in the weighted form of Remark 1.8(1) (lines 298-306, multiplicity θ of Definition 1.7, lines 284-295), localized to one C¹ chart. Parts (B), (C) are Simon Ch. 2, (4.8)-(4.10) (chapter-02.txt lines ≈ 925-957, printed pp. 56-57): Rademacher's theorem in local coordinates and the identification of the tangential directional derivative with the ambient one for f locally Lipschitz on an open set. The book uses these facts in Ch. 3 §2 (lines 343-350: “T_yM agrees with T_yN_j for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M_j” and “D_τf(y) = d/dt f(y + tτ)|_{t=0}”). Detail added: the book argues for embedded submanifolds; we argue on small balls of a C¹ immersion, which is all that is needed (injectivity of ψ on V is not used).

Notation. N = n + ℓ; ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); Hⁿ = μHE[n]; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ (= Hⁿ there); B_ρ(x) open ball, B̄ closed ball; ω_n = Lⁿ(B_1(0)); η_{x,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x); Jψ(u) := normDet(Dψ(u)) = √det(Dψ(u)*Dψ(u)). For x ∈ ℝ^N, λ > 0 and A ⊆ ℝ^N: (F1) ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} g dHⁿ = λ^{-n}∫_A g∘η_{x,λ} dHⁿ for every Borel g ≥ 0 and for every g with g∘η_{x,λ} ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞A) (equivalently g ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞η_{x,λ}(A))), because η_{x,λ} is a similarity of ratio λ⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_{x,λ}(S)) = λ^{-n}Hⁿ(S) for every S (scaling and translation invariance of Hausdorff measure), i.e. (η_{x,λ})_#(Hⁿ⌞A) = λⁿ Hⁿ⌞η_{x,λ}(A). (F2) A K-Lipschitz map does not increase Hⁿ by more than the factor Kⁿ (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), so locally Lipschitz maps on open sets send Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets.

Statement. (Hypotheses as in the Lean statement.) For Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ M: (A) HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (ψ u) (range Dψ(u)); (B) f∘ψ is differentiable at u; (C) ∀ w ∈ ℝⁿ, HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (D(f∘ψ)(u) w) (ψ u) (Dψ(u) w).

Proof.

1. Case n = 0. Then ℝ⁰ = {0} and, if V ≠ ∅, u = 0, Dψ(0) is the zero map on the zero space (injective) with range {0} (finrank 0). H⁰ is counting measure and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ = Σ_{z∈M∩K} θ(z) < ∞ for compact K. For x = ψ(0) ∈ M and f₀ ∈ C_c with spt f₀ ⊆ B_R(0): ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f₀(y)θ(x + λy) dH⁰(y) = Σ_{z∈M} f₀((z − x)/λ) θ(z); for λ ≤ 1 only z ∈ M ∩ B̄_R(x) contribute, the terms are dominated by ‖f₀‖_∞θ(z) (summable), and each term with z ≠ x tends to 0 (|z − x|/λ → ∞), so the sum tends to f₀(0)θ(x) = θ(x)∫_{{0}} f₀ dH⁰. Hence (A) holds. (B) holds since every map on the 0-dimensional space is differentiable, and (C) holds because the only direction is w = 0 and t ↦ f(x + t·0) is constant (derivative 0 = D(f∘ψ)(0)0). Assume n ≥ 1.

2. Localization. For u₀ ∈ V let c₀ := min_{|v|=1}|Dψ(u₀)v| > 0 and choose r₀ = r(u₀) > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(u₀) ⊆ V and ‖Dψ(u) − Dψ(u₀)‖ ≤ c₀/2 on B̄_{2r₀}(u₀) (continuity of Dψ on the open V, ψ being C¹ there). By the mean value inequality on the convex ball, for u, u' ∈ B̄_{2r₀}(u₀): |ψ(u) − ψ(u') − Dψ(u₀)(u − u')| ≤ (c₀/2)|u − u'|, hence (c₀/2)|u − u'| ≤ |ψ(u) − ψ(u')| ≤ Λ|u − u'| with Λ := ‖Dψ(u₀)‖ + c₀/2. So ψ is injective and bi-Lipschitz on B̄_{2r₀}(u₀). V is covered by countably many balls B_{r(uᵢ)}(uᵢ) (Lindelöf), so it suffices to prove (A)-(C) for Lⁿ-a.e. u in one ball B := B_{r₀}(u₀). Put Σ := ψ(B).
 Facts. (Σ1) ψ|B̄_{2r₀}(u₀) is a homeomorphism onto the compact set ψ(B̄_{2r₀}(u₀)), so Σ is relatively open in a compact set, hence Borel. (Σ2) Injective area formula (Simon Ch. 2, (3.2), (4.13); SimonGMT injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn and weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum for the injective Lipschitz map ψ on the open B, where the Jacobian within B is Jψ): ∫_Σ h dHⁿ = ∫_B h(ψ(u)) Jψ(u) du for every Borel h ≥ 0, and hence for bounded Borel h with bounded support (apply it to h⁺ and h⁻; both sides finite); in particular Hⁿ(Σ) < ∞, and for x = ψ(u) ∈ Σ, ρ > 0: Hⁿ(Σ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C₁ρⁿ with C₁ := ω_n (2Λ/c₀)ⁿ (because B ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(x)) ⊆ B̄_{2ρ/c₀}(u) and Jψ ≤ Λⁿ), and Hⁿ(Σ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) > 0 (because B ∩ B_{ρ/Λ}(u) ⊆ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(x)) and Jψ ≥ (c₀/2)ⁿ). (Σ3) For Z ⊆ B: Lⁿ(Z) = 0 iff Hⁿ(ψ(Z)) = 0 (F2 for ψ and for ψ⁻¹ on Σ).

3. Three density properties. Let S := M ∩ Σ (Hⁿ-measurable). Let ν₁ := θHⁿ⌞(M ∖ Σ), i.e. ν₁(A') := ∫_{A' ∩ (M∖Σ)} θ dHⁿ (a Borel regular measure, finite on compact sets by the hypothesis on θ), and ν₂ := Hⁿ⌞(Σ ∖ M) (finite).
 (P1) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S: ρ^{-n}∫_{(M∖Σ)∩B_ρ(x)} θ dHⁿ → 0. This is the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2), chapter-01.txt lines 700-715; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6, simon_remark_3_7_of_openSigmaFinite) applied to the open-σ-finite Borel regular measure ν₁ and the ν₁-measurable set M ∖ Σ: Θ^{*n}(ν₁, M ∖ Σ, x) = 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ M ∖ Σ, in particular for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S (open balls are contained in closed ones).
 (P2) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S: ρ^{-n}Hⁿ((Σ ∖ M) ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0. Same theorem for the finite measure Hⁿ⌞Σ and the set Σ ∖ M (x ∈ S ⇒ x ∉ Σ ∖ M).
 (P3) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S: ρ^{-n}∫_{S∩B_ρ(x)} |θ(z) − θ(x)| dHⁿ(z) → 0. Let λ₀ := Hⁿ⌞Σ (finite Radon measure on ℝ^N) and choose a Borel θ' ≥ 0 with θ' = θ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (θ is Hⁿ⌞M-measurable and positive on M; replace a Borel version by its positive part). Similarly ν₁ may be defined with θ' instead of θ. θ̃ := θ'1_S is λ₀-integrable (∫_S θ ≤ ∫_{M∩ψ(B̄_{2r₀}(u₀))} θ < ∞). By the Lebesgue-Besicovitch differentiation theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Corollary 3.17 with the Symmetric Vitali Property of Radon measures on ℝ^N from Besicovitch's covering lemma 3.12; Mathlib VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily), for λ₀-a.e. x: λ₀(B̄_ρ(x))⁻¹∫_{B̄_ρ(x)}|θ̃ − θ̃(x)| dλ₀ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 (Mathlib states this along the filter VitaliFamily.filterAt; compose with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt to obtain the limit ρ ↓ 0; the denominators are positive by (Σ2)). For such x ∈ S with θ(x) = θ'(x) (all but an Hⁿ-null set of S), using λ₀(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C₁ρⁿ: ρ^{-n}∫_{S∩B_ρ(x)}|θ − θ(x)| dHⁿ ≤ C₁ λ₀(B̄_ρ(x))⁻¹∫_{B̄_ρ(x)}|θ̃ − θ̃(x)| dλ₀ → 0 (the integrands agree Hⁿ-a.e. on S).
 (P4) Blow-up of Σ at every point. For x = ψ(u), u ∈ B, T := range Dψ(u), and f₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) with spt f₀ ⊆ B̄_R(0): λ^{-n}∫_Σ f₀∘η_{x,λ} dHⁿ → ∫_T f₀ dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0. Proof: by (Σ2) and the substitution u' = u + λv,
 λ^{-n}∫_Σ f₀((z − x)/λ) dHⁿ(z) = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{(B−u)/λ}(v) f₀((ψ(u + λv) − ψ(u))/λ) Jψ(u + λv) dv.
 The integrand is bounded by ‖f₀‖_∞Λⁿ and vanishes unless |(ψ(u+λv) − ψ(u))/λ| ≤ R, which by the lower bi-Lipschitz bound forces |v| ≤ 2R/c₀; for fixed v it converges (λ ↓ 0) to f₀(Dψ(u)v)Jψ(u) (B is open; ψ differentiable at u; Jψ continuous; f₀ continuous). Dominated convergence gives the limit Jψ(u)∫_{ℝⁿ} f₀(Dψ(u)v) dv = ∫_T f₀ dHⁿ by the area formula for the injective linear map Dψ(u) (Simon Ch. 2, (3.1): Hⁿ(Dψ(u)(A')) = Jψ(u)Lⁿ(A')).

4. Proof of (A). Let x ∈ S satisfy (P1)-(P3); write x = ψ(u), u ∈ B, T := range Dψ(u) (finrank T = n as Dψ(u) is injective). Fix f₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), spt f₀ ⊆ B_R(0). By (F1) with g(y) := f₀(y)θ(x + λy), so that g∘η_{x,λ}(z) = f₀(η_{x,λ}(z))θ(z) (integrable on M: it is bounded by ‖f₀‖_∞θ and supported in the compact B̄_{Rλ}(x), and θ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B̄_{Rλ}(x)))),
 I(λ) := ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f₀(y) θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) = λ^{-n}∫_M f₀(η_{x,λ}(z)) θ(z) dHⁿ(z).
 Since M = S ⊔ (M ∖ Σ) and λ^{-n}∫_S f₀∘η_{x,λ} = λ^{-n}∫_Σ f₀∘η_{x,λ} − λ^{-n}∫_{Σ∖M} f₀∘η_{x,λ},
 I(λ) = λ^{-n}∫_{M∖Σ} f₀∘η θ + θ(x)[λ^{-n}∫_Σ f₀∘η − λ^{-n}∫_{Σ∖M} f₀∘η] + λ^{-n}∫_S f₀∘η (θ − θ(x)).
 As f₀∘η_{x,λ} vanishes off B_{Rλ}(x) and |f₀| ≤ ‖f₀‖_∞: the first term is ≤ ‖f₀‖_∞ Rⁿ (Rλ)^{-n}∫_{(M∖Σ)∩B_{Rλ}(x)} θ → 0 by (P1); the third bracket term is ≤ ‖f₀‖_∞Rⁿ(Rλ)^{-n}Hⁿ((Σ∖M) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)) → 0 by (P2); the last term is ≤ ‖f₀‖_∞Rⁿ(Rλ)^{-n}∫_{S∩B_{Rλ}(x)}|θ − θ(x)| → 0 by (P3); and λ^{-n}∫_Σ f₀∘η → ∫_T f₀ dHⁿ by (P4). Hence I(λ) → θ(x)∫_T f₀ dHⁿ, which is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T. (Each integrand is a bounded function supported in a compact set, possibly multiplied by θ, which is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K; so all Bochner integrals in the definition are genuine integrals.) The set Z ⊆ S where (P1)-(P3) fail is Hⁿ-null, so ψ⁻¹(Z) ∩ B is Lⁿ-null by (Σ3); every u ∈ B ∖ ψ⁻¹(Z) with ψ(u) ∈ M satisfies (A).

5. Proof of (B) and (C) (Simon Ch. 2, (4.8)-(4.10)). Let u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ U. As U is open and f is locally Lipschitz on U, there are s > 0, L ≥ 0 with B_s(ψ(u)) ⊆ U and f L-Lipschitz on B_s(ψ(u)); choose r > 0 with B̄_r(u) ⊆ V and ψ(B̄_r(u)) ⊆ B_s(ψ(u)). Then f∘ψ is Lipschitz on B̄_r(u); extending it to a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.2, coordinatewise) and applying Rademacher's theorem (Ch. 2, Theorem 1.4; SimonGMT rademacher_ae_differentiableAt) shows f∘ψ is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. point of B_r(u) (differentiability at interior points is local). The open set V ∩ ψ⁻¹(U) is covered by countably many such balls, so (B) holds for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ M ⊆ U.
 (C) holds at every u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ U at which f∘ψ is differentiable: fix w, put x := ψ(u), τ := Dψ(u)w. For small |t|, both x + tτ and ψ(u + tw) lie in B_s(x), so |f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw))| ≤ L|ψ(u) + tDψ(u)w − ψ(u + tw)| = o(t) (differentiability of ψ at u), while f(ψ(u + tw)) = f(x) + tD(f∘ψ)(u)w + o(t). Hence (f(x + tτ) − f(x))/t → D(f∘ψ)(u)w, i.e. HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (D(f∘ψ)(u)w) x τ (this is (4.10) with the curve γ(t) = ψ(u + tw)).

6. Conclusion. The union of the exceptional Lⁿ-null sets of Steps 4 and 5 over the countably many balls of Step 2 is Lⁿ-null, and off it every u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ M satisfies (A), (B), (C). ∎
proof_key_steps: n = 0 is direct (dominated convergence for the counting measure).
Localize to small balls B where ψ is bi-Lipschitz; Σ := ψ(B) is Borel with area formula ∫_Σ h dHⁿ = ∫_B h∘ψ Jψ.
Upper density theorem: θHⁿ⌞(M ∖ Σ) and Hⁿ⌞(Σ ∖ M) have zero n-density at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M ∩ Σ.
Lebesgue differentiation: Hⁿ-a.e. point of M ∩ Σ is a Lebesgue point of θ with the ρⁿ normalization.
Blow-up of the C¹ piece Σ converges to Hⁿ⌞range Dψ(u) at every point (dominated convergence + linear area formula).
Combine via the scaling identity for η_{x,λ} to get (A) off an Lⁿ-null set.
(B) by Rademacher in charts; (C) from differentiability of ψ and the local Lipschitz bound of f (Simon (4.10)).

audit.reason: All chart, weight and ambient Lipschitz hypotheses are present. Local bi-Lipschitz charts, density estimates and chart blow-ups prove the weighted tangent assertion. Rademacher and the explicit o(t) comparison establish the exact two-sided line derivatives, without assuming ambient differentiability.
